title: Hide audit probes and real quantum data from input-based device discrimination
statement: For any correlated rho_DME and a fresh uniform private qubit Pauli key, averaging (P_k tensor I_ME)rho(P_k tensor I_ME) gives I_D/2 tensor rho_ME. An independently uniform six-state test presents the same accessible input through the identical physical call, so any common operation on that input cannot distinguish the roles from those quantum systems. One-bit masking need not seal arbitrary correlations: masking half a Bell pair with{I,X} leaves trace distance1/2 from the test input and equal-prior role-guess success3/4.

The two-bit lower bound is for exact classical random-unitary private qubit encryption; different resource models are not classified here. Biased/reused/exposed keys need their own complete-boundary error law.

body: Here audits are sacrificial test probes, contrasted with real-data USE calls. The input may initially be entangled with retained device memory. Expand the logical operator in the Pauli basis; uniform conjugation kills each nonidentity input coefficient, leaving its partial trace. For the Bell witness, the one-bit mixture is uniform over two orthogonal Bell sectors while the test state is uniform over four, giving half-l1 eigenvalue distance1/2. The carrier marginal is I/2 in both roles and cannot certify joint role privacy. Exact random-unitary depolarization has normalized Choi state I4/4 with entropy2, so the random-key Shannon entropy is at least2 bits within that specified classical random-unitary model; four uniform Paulis attain it. This is established private-quantum-channel mathematics, not a new optimality claim about all cryptographic resources. Correcting a private Pauli after the complete call and retiring the key yields the genuine positive Pauli branch decomposition by character orthogonality. Freshness is conditional on the complete initial payload/reference/apparatus boundary, not a scheduled reuse of a secret pulse. Biased key total variation tau bounds one-call complete-channel half-diamond mismatch and role-input trace distance by tau; that bound does not by itself establish an exact stochastic fault refinement. Finite-block accumulation needs a uniform conditioned bound and pays the sum of allowances. Physical timing/pulse/control/output side channels are outside the quantum masking identity and must actually be sealed.
